synthesis: At positive integer parameters, the random-matrix gamma-product limits defining the symmetry constants can be reorganized into finite factorial and odd-double-factorial products; layerwise p-adic valuation of those products yields exact floor-sum formulas, and geometric sampling k=[p^j x] followed by a shift of valuation scale turns the discrete formulas into a bilateral nearest-integer-square profile. Alongside the second-difference control of the normalized infinite product, this connects one family of constants to analytic continuation, local integrality certificates, and self-similar valuation limits rather than treating it only numerically.
source_support: Unit u03 gives the U, O, and Sp gamma-product limits, preserves the Gamma(1+B_X(lambda)) normalization, and announces integrality and valuation scaling. Unit u05 proves in the unitary case that a second difference of log Gamma cancels the common growth and gives the normalized product exact meromorphic order two. Unit u06 regroups factorial and odd-double-factorial products, applies exact valuation formulas, and proves nonnegative odd-prime valuation layers through exhaustive residue cases. Unit u09 inserts k=[p^j x] into those exact valuations, shifts the layer index, controls finite and tail errors, and identifies the limit with the nearest-integer-square series (with the one-half factor for O and Sp).
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes three representation changes that no single parent supplies: normalized infinite gamma product to integer-specialized finite factorial structure, finite product to prime-and-layer floor sums, and discrete valuation layers to a continuous self-similar scaling profile. It also separates the analytic cancellation performed by second log-Gamma differences from the arithmetic cancellation certified by nonnegative floor-sum layers.
limits: The transfer from random-matrix characteristic polynomials to L-function moments remains conjectural, and agreement at low moments is calibration rather than proof. The detailed order-two argument in u05 is shown for U with the other symmetry cases called similar. The displayed valuation-positivity proof in u06 treats odd primes; p=2 is only set aside as easy. The scaling result is along k=[p^j x], uses exact floor conventions, and does not assert arbitrary-sequence convergence.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct exact parent units jointly support a concrete, source-explicit chain from the gamma-product definition through finite-product valuation certificates to a geometric scaling limit. The relation adds a mechanism unavailable from any parent alone while retaining the source's conjectural-transfer, symmetry-case, prime-2, sampling, and notation boundaries.
